@ a when~ written inside the part reads the time of the frame of its tick: the ticks at 0 2 6 13 read 0 2 6 13, true at 0 and 6 and false at 13
process 0 frames=16 in c=[true true true false true false true false false false false true false true true false]
@ a reset_if~ written inside the part reads the same time: the part is put back at the ticks 0 and 6, not at 13
process 0 frames=16 in c=[true true true false true false true false false false false true false true true false]
@ the time since a start written inside the part is the time of the frame: a note of 13 frames from 0 is off at the tick 13
process 0 params t0=0 len=13 frames=16 in c=[true true true false true false true false false false false true false true true false]
@ a modifier at W = sample reads the time of the frame: a when~ runs on the frames that run whose time is a multiple of 3, and a reset_if~ puts back there
process 0 frames=16 in c=[true true true false true false true false false false false true false true true false]
process 1 frames=16 in c=[true true true false true false true false false false false true false true true false]
@ a burst read at W = sample * 2 takes the condition as a value of the body's sample: the time of the frame, true at 0 3 6 9 12 15
@ no when~ outside the block: the ticks are the even frames and the time kept is the time of the frame: 1 2 2 2 2 2 3 4 4 4 4 4 5 6 6 6
@ the time as the argument of the head is the time of the frame that runs: the part holds at the frames that are stopped
process 0 frames=16 in c=[true true true false true false true false false false false true false true true false]
